strategy.cost: No subscription minimum, key or new account for tested public endpoints. Hosting/cache execution is separate. No SLA claimed.
strategy.recommended: Expand client selector using server-cached dated reference quotes. Keep ECB named source mode, add broader Frankfurter source mode with its actual provider provenance. Do not call every broader quote ECB.
strategy.formula: When rates are quote units per1base unit: amount*rate[to]/rate[from]. NBP mid is PLN per1foreign unit: amount*mid[from]/mid[to].
strategy.dates: Keep observedDate perquote and fetchedAt separately. Cross-date conversion must show both dates; strict historical mode needs same supported observation date. Weekend/publication lag is normal; use source-specific stale policy, never change observedDate tofetchdate.
strategy.provenance: Preserve contributing provider IDs, own dates, excluded flags, and peg-derived status; current response includes stale source observation as early Sep29 inside Oct9blend. Do not represent row date as every contributor date.
strategy.cache: Bounded server fetch timeout; validate full snapshot then atomically replace; keep last-known-good tagged stale; missing currency disables only that pair; no secret inclient. On upstream outage manualrate remains available.
strategy.precision: Do not round intermediate conversion; test tiny quote rates (metals, high-denominationfiat), and prefer robust direct or inverse pair rates if feed rounding introduces materialerror.
strategy.currentLimit: 164observed competitor instruments have current feed rows; six missing are legacy-only; BTC andCLF need distinct adapters. 223advertisedincludeslegacy, not223currentcurrencies.
strategy.terms: Frankfurter docs explicitly permit free commercial API use but underlying rates retain each provider terms. Review chosen provider terms; no blanket licence inference. NBP metadata terms_url null does not mean public domain.
strategy.excludedSource: UN operational exchange rates explicitly intended for internal UN accounting, not a public market-rate fallback.
